items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: it’s linear, it’s Don Cherry, it’s World Saxophone Quartet

ctx.x: Well you can overdo that for sure. I mean the whole point of it is there are no chords. Jazz is a counterpoint between the bass and the melody. And you know, the chords are implied by that counterpoint. You know, the true jazz musician doesn’t pay attention to vertical constructs. Okay, C seven [scats], okay, B flat seven. I mean you’re not supposed to. I mean that’s not the point. That’s popular music. You know jazz music is linear, it’s linear, it’s Don Cherry, it’s World Saxophone Quartet, it’s —
Even Ellington, his writing was more like that. He had all those lines going on.
